steps: Check the hearth
The non-combustible masonry hearth must extend 16" in front of and 8" beyond each side of the fireplace opening. Minimum fireplace opening sizes are shown only as a diagram (Figure 3).
Ember protection
Cover combustible flooring with non-combustible material: 16" (USA) or 18" (Canada) to the firing side, measured from the glass, plus 8" to each side.

USA16" to the firing side (from the glass) · 8" to each side of the door opening
Canada18" to the firing side (from the glass) · 8" to each side of the unit

Consult CAN/CSA-B365 (Canada) or N.F.P.A. 211 (USA). Figure 4 shows the layout as a diagram.
Clearances to combustibles
From the blower covers: 10" to an adjacent sidewall and 6" to side facing (max 3-1/2" deep). From the cast top: 12" to mantel facing and to a mantel (max 12" deep).
Prepare the fireplace
Masonry wood-burning fireplace only, with a chimney 15' minimum from the hearth, swept, inspected and repaired first. Lock the damper open or remove it; never share the flue with another appliance.

• Built to N.F.P.A. 211 or applicable codes; installation per CAN/CSA-B365. No makeshift or temporary installs.
  • Check for creosote and obstructions; repair cracks, loose mortar or other defects before installing.
  • Don't remove bricks or mortar. Exception: masonry or steel, including the damper plate, may be removed from the smoke shelf and adjacent damper frame to fit a liner, if that doesn't weaken the fireplace and chimney or reduce protection for combustibles below the National Building Code.
  • If the fireplace was modified, fasten the supplied metal tag to its back wall.
  • The insert is heavy: install with two people, with cardboard or a heavy blanket protecting the hearth.
Run the liner (required in Canada)

Continuous stainless steel liner from the top of the chimney into the fireplace cavity, with a stove-to-liner adapter. Attach the flue collar with three stainless screws and caulk with high temp stove cement.

1. Measure from the top of the existing chimney flue to the floor of the hearth; this leaves extra liner for flashing and rain cap.
  2. Feed the liner from the top, through the damper area, into the fireplace cavity. Attach a "stove to liner" adapter per the liner manufacturer.
  3. Attach the flue collar (packed in the stove) to the adapter with three stainless screws, caulk with high temp stove cement and check the gasket.

Canada: class 3 liner per CAN/ULC-B365 or CAN/ULC-S640 (this page); the rating label names CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640. See the conflict note under Chimney & flue.
Or: direct flue connection (USA only)
Liner from the first chimney flue tile down to the insert, sealed where it passes the chimney throat; a clean-out door may be required by local code. Then follow full-liner steps 3-9.

Measure from the first chimney flue liner tile to the top of the insert, allowing extra liner to go into the flue tile. Feed the stainless steel liner through the damper area into the first flue tile, fit a "stove to liner" adapter and seal around the liner in the chimney throat.

Pacific Energy highly recommends a full liner as the safest installation with the best performance.
Set, level & connect

Remove the cast top, both blower covers and the baffle; push the insert in and level it. Pull the collar down through the flue opening, clamp and tighten it, then flash the chimney top and fit a rain cap.

1. Cast top: lift up at the front and pull toward you. Blower covers: lift up and pull toward you to release the tabs.
  2. Remove the baffle.
  3. Push the unit in and level it with the front or rear adjustment legs: rear bolts if the fireplace is lower than the hearth, front bolts if the hearth is lower than the fireplace floor (p. 13).
  4. Reach through the flue opening and pull the collar down with the tool provided until the bolts pass through the mounting holes. Fit clamps and nuts, center the collar and tighten.
  5. Trim and shape a chimney-top flashing with a 1" to 1-1/2" overlap on each side; seat it firmly on the flue tile over the liner.
  6. Attach a rain cap to the end of the liner (storm collar optional).
  7. Install the surround, then refit the top and blower covers.
Combustion air & power
Outside air through the fireplace ash clean-out (rodent screen, surround sealed) or room air (Room Air Cover removed). Blowers need 115V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A from a grounded three-prong outlet.

• Outside air: keep the insert's air inlet uncovered and seal the surround to the fireplace and anywhere else air may enter.
  • Room air: remove the decorative cover under the ash lip (two screws), discard the Room Air Cover, refit the decorative cover.
  • Power cord: never under the unit, clear of hot or sharp surfaces; don't cut the grounding prong.
Surround & final fit
Assemble the surround, test-fit it with the fan shields and cast top, and check door clearance. Remove it, lift the insert into place, reinstall the surround and tighten it to the mounting studs.

If the fan speed control has to move to the left side, do it before fitting the surround (p. 21).

  1. Uncrate and place the insert where you can reach its back.
  2. Lift off the top; support the fan shields (they may fall) and lift them off.
  3. Unpack the surround top and sides (this step is marked porcelain enamel only).
  4. Move the surround brackets onto the surround sides with the bolts and washers from the kit packed with the surround top.
  5. Lay the sides flat on a blanket, square them to the surround top and bolt the brackets. Oversized surround: use mounting holes (K).
  6. Angle the sides behind the ash shelf, slot the brackets over the studs and fasten with washers and nuts.
  7. Fit the fan shields with the air inlet opening to the back, against the surround side.
  8. Slide the cast decorative top under the surround top and over the casing top, engaging the fan shields in its slots.
  9. Check panel fit and door clearance, tighten all bolts, remove the panel set, lift the insert in, reinstall the surround and tighten it to the studs.

panels.title: Creosote buildup or dirty glass
items: Wood too wet → use dry wood
Air turned down too soon → wait for a good bed of coals and charred wood
Draft too low → check chimney height / diameter and for a plugged or restricted flue; provide outside air
Dirty glass only: door gasket leakage → replace gasket, check latch

panels.title: Low heat output
items: Wood is wet → use dry wood
Fire too small → build a larger fire

panels.title: Won't burn overnight
items: Air control set too high → set control lower
Not enough wood → un-split wood is preferred
Possible air leak → door gasket needs changing

items: Combustion air supply blocked → check outside air supply for obstructions
Draft too low: chimney plugged or restricted → inspect and clean
Chimney oversized or otherwise unsuitable → consult dealer

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
You light this insert by hand, with newspaper and kindling. The manual's sequence:

  1. Move the air control to High (all the way to the left) and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the firebox and crisscross several pieces of dry kindling over it. Add a few small pieces of dry wood on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open a crack, about 1/2" (13mm) to 1" (25mm), until the kindling is fully engulfed in flame.
  4. Add a few small logs and close the door.
  5. Switch to normal burning once there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred.
Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or any other chemical or volatile liquid to start or freshen up a fire. Keep all such liquids well away from the insert while it's in use.
Hot while in operation. Keep children, clothing and furniture away; contact may cause skin burns.

Your first few fires

The paint bakes on during the first 2-3 fires. Keep the room well ventilated, with windows and doors open; the smoke and fumes can bother some people. Follow the Stove Bright paint sheet that came with the stove. Smoke detectors may go off more often while the paint cures. Don't disconnect them.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
One air control sets how hard the fire burns: High is all the way to the left, Low (L) is pushed to the far right.

  • Once the fire is going, set it where you want it. Every home's heating needs differ, so finding your setting takes trial and error. Note it for next time.
  • Smoke pouring down across the glass (a "waterfall") means you turned it down too soon or set it too low.
  • Leave it relatively wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes after each load, when most smoke forms. After 30 minutes or so you can turn it down a lot.
  • Use the full High setting only to start the fire or preheat a fresh load.
Don't over-fire. A top or vent pipe glowing red means the insert is over-firing. That can permanently damage the insert and chimney and may void the warranty. A burn you can't control, or a stove part or chimney glowing red, also points to too much draft.
The minimum burn rate is set at the factory. Altering it is against federal regulations, and tampering with the air control voids the warranty.

reload.title: Reloading & overnight burns
reload.html:
Adding wood

  1. Move the air control to High and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly. That prevents back puffing (smoke puffing back into the room).
  3. Load the wood endwise, placing the logs so air can flow between them. Different shapes and sizes are fine, up to 18" (457mm) long. Always use dry wood.
  4. Don't stack wood so high, or in such a way, that opening the door would be hazardous.
Always keep the loading door closed when burning. This heater isn't designed for open-door burning; sparks, embers or smoke can come out.

Overnight burns

Unsplit logs work best. Char the load completely on the maximum setting before you turn the air down for the night. Don't try to burn overnight with green or wet wood.

Restarting in the morning

Open the door and rake the hot embers toward the front. Add a couple of dry, split logs on top and close the door. Set the air to High; the logs should start burning in a few minutes. Once the wood has charred, reset the air control.

Won't burn overnight? The manual's checklist: air control set too high, not enough wood (unsplit is better), or an air leak that means the door gasket needs changing.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood gives higher efficiency and lower emissions than softwood or green, freshly cut hardwood.

  • Season wood for six months or more, and store it under cover, away from open flame or heat. Don't store it within the insert's clearances or in the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.

Test a piece

Add a large piece to a good, large bed of coals. Burning on more than one side within one minute: dry. Turns black and lights within three minutes: damp. Sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes: soaked, so don't burn it.

Never burn

Salt water wood, treated wood, wet, green or unseasoned wood, garbage, coal or charcoal, solvents, lawn clippings or yard waste, railroad ties, manure or animal remains, anything containing rubber (including tires), plastic or asbestos, construction or demolition debris, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners or asphalt products, or paper products, cardboard, plywood or particleboard. Salt water wood and garbage contain chlorides that rapidly destroy metal and void the warranty. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes, or make the insert ineffective and cause smoke.

Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting.

Note: p. 6 lists wet, green and unseasoned wood as wood not to burn, then p. 7 says that if you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air inlet set open enough to maintain a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures. It also says not to attempt to burn overnight using green wood or wet wood.
Never barbecue in this heater. Charcoal and other fuels can produce large amounts of carbon monoxide, an odourless gas that can kill.

blower.title: Using the blowers
blower.html:
Two variable-speed blowers circulate warm air into the room. You run them with a rocker switch and a speed control, which is factory-fitted under the ash lip on the right-hand side.

Rocker switch OffAutomatic: the blowers come on once the insert is up to temperature, and shut off after the fire is out and it has cooled
Rocker switch OnManual: bypasses the temperature switch for full control

Either way, set the speed control to the speed you want.

Suggested settings

  • Air control at L (low, pushed to the far right): run the blowers on Low.
  • Air control anywhere above L: any blower speed you like.

Keep them clean

Vacuum the blower intakes at least every six months to clear dust and debris. Reaching them means lifting off the decorative top and the fan shields (steps 1 and 2 of the fan speed controller section on p. 21).

Risk of electrical shock: disconnect power before servicing the unit.

glass.title: Cleaning the door glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass with fireplace glass cleaner, and only when the stove is cold.

  • Never scrape it with anything that might scratch, and don't use abrasive cleaners.
  • Don't slam the door. When you close it, make sure no logs stick out to hit the glass.

What the deposit tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good combustion, dry wood and relatively clean pipes and chimney. A black, greasy deposit that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly, and it's building up at least as fast in the chimney.

Glass getting dirty fast? The troubleshooting chart points to wet wood, turning the air down too soon, low draft, or a leaking door gasket or latch.

Cracked or broken glass must be replaced before you use the stove. Use only 17-1/4" (438mm) x 11-3/8" (289mm) x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer. Don't substitute any other type.

Plated door: mild soap and water only. Abrasive cleaners void the warranty.

ash.title: Removing the ashes
ash.html:
Empty ashes only when the heater is cold, after the fire has burned down and cooled.

  • Remove the excess whenever ashes get 3" (76mm) to 4" (102mm) deep in the firebox.
  • Leave an ash bed about 1" (25 mm) deep on the firebox bottom. It helps keep a hot charcoal bed.
  • Keep the front of the firebox clear of heavy ash buildup. That's where boost air comes in, and ash can block it.

Safe disposal

Put the ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set the closed container on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn, until final disposal. If you bury or spread them, keep them in the closed container until every cinder has thoroughly cooled. Don't put other waste in that container.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow, smoky fires leave creosote, a tar-like residue that builds up in the chimney. If it ignites, it makes an extremely hot chimney fire.

  • Inspect the chimney connector and chimney at least once every two months in the heating season, and remove creosote once it reaches 3 mm or more.
  • Check daily for creosote buildup until experience shows you how often you need to clean to be safe.
  • The maintenance checklist also recommends checking the liner and connector monthly, and having the liner cleaned annually or more often if needed.
  • To keep it down: burn dry wood, use small loads (two or three logs at a time), and keep the air relatively wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes after loading.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Get ready to evacuate, with a meeting place outside.
  2. Close the air inlet on the stove.
  3. Call the fire department and keep a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Before the next fire, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks, and check combustibles around the chimney and roof.
Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended in the area where the heater is installed.

care.title: Maintenance checks
care.html:
Check these parts for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and excessive warping.

WeeklyFirebrick (cracks) · door gasket (sagging, placement, damage)
MonthlyBaffle and its locking pin · brick rails and tabs · air riser tube · back of the airwash chamber · boost tube cover · liner and connector
At chimney cleaningTop baffle board/blanket · top heat shield and bolt · baffle gasket · brick rails · manifold
At least every six monthsVacuum the blower intakes

Door gasket

The 5/16" medium density fiberglass rope gasket needs only light pressure to seal. Inspect it periodically and replace it when needed, using the kit from your Pacific Energy dealer.

Baffle

Some warping is normal, up to 1/4" (6.5mm). Replace it if it's permanently warped more than that, cracked or broken. Never run the stove with the baffle or its insulation removed.

Found damage? Contact your dealer. Running the stove with broken parts can damage other parts and may void your warranty. Use only materials supplied by the manufacturer.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's wood products warranty goes to the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years)Parts only: porcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage, not impact), plating, firebox and baffle
3 year comprehensiveParts and labor on any defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets; firebox rails and heat shields are left out of the lifetime coverage
  • Labor under the lifetime coverage
  • Parts showing misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification

Tampering with the air control, burning salt water wood or garbage, and abrasive cleaners on the plated door void it; over-firing may too. Porcelain can darken when hot and return to its shade when cool.

Making a claim

Go to your dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number. The serial number is on the certification label (bottom back corner of the side casing, door-catch side) or on the manual's cover. Register online at pacificenergy.net/register.

specFuel.title: Fuel & wood length
specFuel.html:
FuelSeasoned cord wood
Ideal wood length16 inches
Maximum wood length18 inches

Solid wood fuel only; the stove is designed to burn cordwood only. No grate or andirons: build the fire directly on the firebricks. Load endwise, up to 18"(457mm) (p. 7).

specEpa.title: Emissions & efficiency
specEpa.html:
EPA certified emissions1.8 grams per hour
HHV tested efficiency71%
LHV tested efficiency77%
Maker's website: Efficiency (HHV) 71.3%.

Weighted-average efficiencies, tested using CSA B415. Certified to the 2020 EPA crib wood particulate emission standards using test Method 28R. The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered (p. 7).

specOutput.title: Heat output
specOutput.html:
EPA BTU output (table)12,518 to 38,177 btu/hr
Test-condition range (text)16,102 to 41,275 Btu/hr
Maker's website: Heat Output (Cord Wood) 72,000 BTU.

The table's range is based on efficiency and burn rates from the low and high EPA tests, using Douglas Fir dimensional lumber.

Note: p. 3 gives the heat output two ways: its Efficiency and BTU Output table gives an EPA BTU output of 12,518 to 38,177 btu/hr, and the same page says that under specific test conditions the heater has been shown to deliver heat at rates ranging from 16,102 to 41,275 Btu/hr.

specHearth.html:
Masonry hearth, in front of opening16"
Masonry hearth, beyond each side of opening8"
Ember protection, USA16" to the firing side (from the glass) · 8" to each side of the door opening
Ember protection, Canada18" to the firing side (from the glass) · 8" to each side of the unit

The hearth must be non-combustible masonry (p. 12). Ember protection is non-combustible material over combustible flooring in front of the insert. Rating label: firing side 406 MM / 16 IN (U.S.A.) and 457 MM / 18 IN (Canada), other sides 200 MM / 8 IN. Consult CAN/CSA-B365 in Canada and N.F.P.A. 211 in the USA. Figure 4 on p. 13 shows the layout as a diagram.

specFlue.title: Chimney & flue
specFlue.html:
FireplaceMasonry wood-burning fireplace only
Flue collar6" I.D., removable
Chimney height (from hearth)15' (minimum)
CanadaContinuous full flue liner, flue collar to top of chimney
USAFlue liner conforming to UL-1777, or a direct flue connection assembly

Do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance. Lock the existing damper open or remove it. Pacific Energy highly recommends a full liner: the insert drafts correctly and it prevents difficult start-ups and smoking out the door (p. 17).

Note: for the liner in Canada, the rating label on p. 3 calls for a full flue liner conforming to CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640; p. 16 says the liner must meet the class 3 requirements of CAN/ULC-B365 (named there as the standard for lining systems for existing masonry or factory-built chimneys and vents) or CAN/ULC-S640.
Note: p. 14 introduces the clearances as applying when the insert is installed into a masonry or factory built fireplace, but the rating label (p. 3) and p. 15 say the insert is not to be installed in any factory-built fireplace.

specElec.title: Electrical & combustion air
specElec.html:
Blower electrical rating115V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A
OutletProperly grounded, for a three-pronged plug
BlowersTwin variable speed, thermostatically controlled, with bypass switch

Don't cut or remove the grounding prong or route the cord under the unit; keep it clear of hot or sharp surfaces. Wire to local code, or CSA C22.2 (Canada) / ANSI/NFPA 70 (USA). Disconnect power before servicing.

Combustion air

  • Outside air: replace the fireplace ash clean-out cover with a rodent screen, keep the air inlet uncovered, then seal the surround to the fireplace and anywhere else air may enter. Air is drawn into the intake on the bottom of the appliance.
  • Room air: remove the two screws holding the decorative cover under the ash lip, remove and discard the Room Air Cover from the base bottom, refit the decorative cover. Air is drawn from the room through the front.

Fan service

The fan speed controller is factory installed under the ash lip on the right and can be moved to the left; it's easiest before the surround is fitted (p. 21). To replace a fan, remove the decorative top and fan shields, disconnect that fan's wires (and the thermal switch if needed), then remove the two bracket screws with a 7/16" socket or wrench (p. 24).

conflicts.issue: Heat output: the Efficiency and BTU Output table gives an EPA BTU output of 12,518 to 38,177 btu/hr; the text on the same page says that under specific test conditions the heater delivers heat at rates ranging from 16,102 to 41,275 Btu/hr.

Canadian liner standard: the rating label requires a full flue liner conforming to CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640; p. 16 requires the class 3 requirements of CAN/ULC-B365 ('Standard for Lining Systems for Existing Masonry or Factory-Built Chimneys and Vents') or CAN/ULC-S640.

Fireplace type: p. 14 says the clearances apply 'when installed into a masonry or factory built fireplace'; the rating label (p. 3) and p. 15 say the insert is not to be installed in any factory-built fireplace.
Adjacent sidewall clearance in mm: 10 in. (245 mm.) in the p. 14 clearance list, 254mm in Figure 5 on p. 14, 255 MM / 10 IN on the rating label (p. 3). Inch value consistent.

Wet and unseasoned wood: p. 6 lists 'Wet or green wood' and 'Unseasoned wood' under DO NOT BURN; p. 7 says 'If you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air inlet set open enough to maintain a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures' and 'Do not attempt to burn overnight using green wood or wet wood'. The guide shows both in an amber note in the wood drawer.

review.notes: Two catalog models share this manual (100003038, rev 061124-32). The manual never uses the name 'Classic': its cover and rating label say only 'Alderlea T5 LE Insert' / 'Alderlea T5 Insert LE'. It tells the versions apart only by finish: the parts list (p. 28) gives each visible casting (top, crown, fan shields, ash lip, door) as Painted / Met Black, Majolica Brown Enamel or Antique White Enamel, and surround step 3 (p. 19) is marked 'porcelain enamel only'. Every performance, clearance, hearth, venting and electrical number is shared, so per-version rows appear only in the castings card, labelled by finish as the manual does (the catalog maps Classic to the porcelain enamel finishes and the T5 Insert LE to metallic black). The rating label on p. 3 (Figure 1, label 100002100) is shared with the Super Insert LE, and several listed parts are Super LE parts. The Efficiency and BTU Output table on p. 3 is printed rotated and its extracted text is scrambled; the pairing used (HHV 71%, LHV 77%, ideal 16 inches, maximum 18 inches, EPA output 12,518 to 38,177 btu/hr, 1.8 grams per hour) was confirmed from column alignment in the page-layout text.
